headToHead.ours: script-r1 ep-05, Tilly (booth C): "If they pick me, I'll get a break. I don't know what you do in one."
headToHead.bar: Animal Crossing #9, Lazy: "If I stay here long enough, I'll probably have to start shaving."
headToHead.verdict: Charm on a level with the bar, and it's a want. But it tells a bettor nothing about the star and it is the second 'if they pick' line in two windows. Bar.

headToHead.ours: hybrid-02 ep-01, Brock (booth B): "I just want to hear 'good job, Brock.' Once. I'd frame it. I don't have walls."
headToHead.bar: Love Island Beach Hut: a short bite to the lens that is ironised by the next scene (here, Brock is cut the very next round)
headToHead.verdict: The pathos and the irony with his cut both work. Structurally, though, a Beach Hut bite is about the person in the room; this one is about Brock's bio. Bar.

headToHeadSummary: As jokes, our six best one-liners nearly match Monster Prom. As a beat, they lose clearly to the Beach Hut. A Beach Hut bite reacts to a moment the viewer just saw, says the opposite of what the islander says to the person's face, and gets proved wrong or right on screen. Our booth lines are freestanding character gags. They almost never cite anything the star said, and they call the star an anonymous 'they'. Only one (Dash, ep-04) gets a payoff.

bankNotes: Personas whose booth lines need rewriting: Crumb (stat lines invent events; it needs stats about what just happened on screen), Nav (references to predictions and secrets the viewer never saw), Tilly (bio-dump confessions), Prince (gags with no want), Sir Quill (one elegy line is doing double duty across episodes), Dash (rival reads with no metric turn). The booth needs a 'read' line type for every persona: what I think the star's last line to me meant, which may be wrong.
pickMakesSense: Not for this beat. Speakers seem chosen at random from the survivors: Quill, the eventual winner in ep-01, gets no booth-B line; the star speaks in the booth in hybrid-02 ep-01. Lines are chosen by reaction type (charmed/cringing), not by the star's actual words, so they contradict what just aired (ep-02 Crumb, ep-03 Brock, ep-04 Quill).
biggestGap: The booth never reads the star. A Beach Hut bite is an islander's read of the person they want, often wrong and soon proved so. Ours are freestanding bio gags about an anonymous 'they', and not one quotes or interprets the star's actual reaction line. So the bettor gets no signal and the next round can't pay anything off. Every booth line should be built from the star's last line to that suitor plus the suitor's in-voice guess at what it means. For example, Dash: "'Except bingo.' She said bingo. Bingo is numbers. Doubling down on numbers." That guess is right or wrong against the hidden cards, and the reveal settles it.
structuralChange: Make the booth a replay-and-read, with two bites per window of about 10 to 12 seconds each, and keep the star out. Window B, just after the cut: replay the star's most ambiguous reaction from round one as a 2-second audio sting. Then the suitor it was aimed at reads it in the booth, and a rival gives the opposite read. One of them is right about a hidden card, and the reveal later shows the replay again with a tick or a cross. Window C: only the two who will reach the one-on-one speak. Each says one line they will not say to the star's face. Then the one-on-one opens with that suitor saying the opposite to the star (the Beach Hut contradiction cut). Drop the mirrored 'if my rival wins' pair, which runs in window C in three of eight episodes, with a mutual about-each-other pair in a fourth. Ban reusing a booth line within a 10-episode run.
